conventions: ha-ish ha-hu and ha-nephesh ha-hiv (20.3, 20.4, 20.5, 20.6): the ASV writes one determiner, that, for the whole phrase, and the written pronoun hu/hiv takes it under rule 18, leaving both articles - the one on the noun and the one on the demonstrative - unrepresented under rule 41's limit. The competing reading fuses article and pronoun into one unit for the single word, which is how the corpus reads ha-hu at 1KI.10.10 (these); it was not taken here, because the pronoun is written and rule 41 gives the determiner to the morpheme that licenses it.

Distributive ish ish (20.2, 20.9): the count of English words decides, not the construction. At 20.2 the ASV writes one word for the pair (Whosoever he be), so the first occurrence carries Whosoever he and the second is unrepresented under rule 22; at 20.9 it writes a word for each (every one), so rule 2 splits them one to one. The difference between the two verses is the ASV's and is not an inconsistency.

A coordinating and the ASV supplies before a le + infinitive phrase it has recast as a coordinate clause is its own added unit and never the lamed's: 20.4 (and put him not to death) and 20.16 (and lie down thereto) were both corrected to this reading, the lamed going unrepresented under rule 40. Rule 14's closing sentence and rule 52's inventory are what forbid making a preposition the home for a coordinator; rule 26's contrary treatment reaches only the beyn X le-Y connective, which neither of these is.

The casuistic asher of the death-penalty series takes the ASV's if (20.12, 20.13, 20.14, 20.15, 20.16, 20.17, 20.18, 20.20, 20.21): a written relative stands in each clause, so rule 55's count marks nothing added. Where the ASV keeps a relative instead (20.2, 20.6, 20.10, 20.11) the same morpheme takes that, and at 20.10 the second asher additionally takes the supplied antecedent under rule 46's rider (he that).

ov heads on familiar in both its renderings - have familiar spirits (20.6) and a familiar spirit (20.27) - since spirit alone is any spirit under rule 31's subtraction. The supplied have of 20.6 belongs to the noun's own periphrasis, no hayah or possessive morpheme standing in that clause, whereas 20.27's hath is hayah's under rule 43.

The waw at 20.23 takes and therefore as one rendering written at its clause's left edge, on the model of rule 55's coordinator-plus-subordinator pair, rather than taking and alone with therefore left added under rule 51's count. Rule 55's sentence names a subordinator and this is a conjunctive adverb, so the reading is an extension of it; elsewhere in the chapter a waw for which the ASV writes therefore alone takes just that word (20.7, 20.22, 20.25).
report: Read all 27 verses end to end against the 56 candidate groups, and swept the dump separately for the split the lemma table is blind to: a supplied English word marked added in one verse and folded into a neighbouring morpheme in another. The chapter holds three added units (20.4 and, 20.10 even, 20.16 and) and nowhere folds a supplied word of that kind into a neighbour. The two coordinators are one correction applied identically in both verses; the appositional even at 20.10 stands in a clause whose two et tokens are both MACULA-tagged R, so no marker was passed over.

Closest candidates, each licensed by what the ASV wrote rather than a split: the distributive ish ish (20.2 one English word for the pair, second occurrence unrepresented under rule 22; 20.9 a word for each, split under rule 2) turns on rule 30's one-English-word count; asher rendered if in the casuistic series against that elsewhere is the ASV's own recasting; ha-ish ha-hu and ha-nephesh ha-hiv are handled identically in 20.3, 20.4, 20.5 and 20.6; preposition-plus-construct fusion is decided by rule 30's subtraction every time, so mi-qerev to from among splits while be-tokh to among and mi-pene to before fuse; and le + 1cs splits at 20.26 s003 (unto me) but fuses at s019 (mine) inside one verse, exactly as rule 49's last clause directs.

BSB: 24 disagreements, none a genuine error. Five are prepositions the ASV's recasting leaves nothing to say (the le of lemor at 20.1 under rule 27; the lameds of levilti hamit and lerivah; ba-m at 20.23, whose object the ASV promotes to a bare direct object; ba-hem at 20.27 under the possessive recasting). Seven articles, four of them bracketed assimilated tokens, and eight object markers are the documented convention difference. The remaining four are the second ish of the 20.2 distributive pair, the suffix of shekhovto at 20.15 which the fused lie leaves nothing for, the apodosis waw at 20.16 for which the ASV writes no connective, and the suffix of ba-hem at 20.27. All are convention, not correction.

Six conventions recorded: the chapter had none in its log while 88 notes repeat, so every chapter-wide judgment below reached its later verses without being written down. No promotion: the one candidate worth promoting - that a written hu takes the demonstrative determiner before its own article does - is contradicted by the corpus, which aligns ha + hu as a single unit for these at 1KI.10.10, so it stays a convention. The rest restate rules 14, 22, 30, 41, 52 and 55.

One thin spot for a later reader: 20.23's waw takes and therefore as a single rendering at the clause's left edge. Rule 55's pair sentence names a coordinator plus a subordinator, and therefore is a conjunctive adverb, so the case sits just outside the wording; rule 51's count would instead leave therefore added. One occurrence and no corpus counts in the packet, so it is recorded rather than promoted.
